ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale, granular belly. Key features include a rounded snout, distinct tympanum, and webbed toes with enlarged, rounded tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana polunini* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped glandular warts on its back, which are absent in most other similar *Nanorana* species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana polunini* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,000 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Langtang Paa frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, high-altitude streams of the Himalayas.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana polunini* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in high-altitude mountain streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana polunini* is found in the high-altitude Himalayas of Nepal and India (Sikkim and Uttarakhand), typically occurring at elevations between 2,500 and 4,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Langtang Paa Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its high-altitude Himalayan habitat.
